exampleAnswers.Purpose and audience: A pricing worksheet that normalizes plan assumptions and makes missing costs visible.
exampleAnswers.Working context: This fictional comparison uses three invented software plans for a five-person team. The amounts are illustrative EUR monthly prices, not current vendor offers.
exampleAnswers.Example records:
Plan: Basic · Base EUR/month: 20 · Included seats: 2 · Extra seat EUR: 8 · Five-seat total EUR: 44
Plan: Team · Base EUR/month: 45 · Included seats: 5 · Extra seat EUR: 6 · Five-seat total EUR: 45
Plan: Studio · Base EUR/month: 70 · Included seats: 10 · Extra seat EUR: 5 · Five-seat total EUR: 70
exampleAnswers.Content decisions:
Normalize the basis: The Basic example costs €44 for five people: €20 plus three extra seats at €8. Team costs €45 and Studio costs €70 at the same team size.
Beyond the headline: Compare required features, storage limits, billing commitments, support, export options, and any usage charges. A one-euro difference is not meaningful if an option cannot meet the actual requirement.
Before a purchase: Replace the sample plans with verified current quotes and record their dates, currency, and tax basis. Recalculate if the team size or billing term changes.
exampleAnswers.Format and interaction: comparison layout; section navigation and expandable detail where useful; matching portrait document PDF.
exampleAnswers.Sharing and provenance: A hypothetical example informed by Claw Me’s small-team and Agent workflows. These are not Pete’s actual clients, finances, travel plans, research results, or commitments. Keep the real adaptation private until the owner chooses to share.
